correlates.name: Post-Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
correlates.pathophysiology: hemodynamic changes after acute MI drive high RAAS activity, and angiotensin II promotes ventricular remodeling.
correlates.treatment: an ACE inhibitor or ARB improves mortality in randomized trials, especially after ST-elevation MI (Slides 36, 45).

correlates.name: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
correlates.pathophysiology: neprilysin inhibition raises natriuretic peptides, bradykinin, and substance P, which are natriuretic, vasodilatory, and antiproliferative in their own right.
correlates.treatment: ACE inhibitor, ARB, or the neprilysin inhibitor-ARB combination sacubitril-valsartan (the only one marketed), given with a beta blocker, plus a loop diuretic if fluid control is needed (Slide 36).

correlates.name: Proteinuric Chronic Kidney Disease (Diabetic and Non-Diabetic)
correlates.pathophysiology: three layers - lowering systemic blood pressure (which every antihypertensive does), dilating the efferent arteriole to drop intraglomerular pressure (which only RAS inhibitors do), and reducing protein excretion. Other intrarenal mechanisms are likely.
correlates.treatment: ACE inhibitors and ARBs slow progression of both forms (Slide 36).

correlates.name: ACE Inhibitor Cough
correlates.presentation: persistent dry, non-productive cough starting after the drug is begun. Not dangerous - but bothersome enough to end therapy.
correlates.pathophysiology: accumulation of bradykinin, substance P, and probably prostaglandins in the lungs, irritating the airway (Slide 38).
correlates.treatment: switch to an ARB; incidence with ARBs is low but not zero.

correlates.name: ACE Inhibitor-Induced Angioedema
correlates.presentation: swelling of lips, tongue, face, or airway - rare but potentially fatal.
correlates.pathophysiology: bradykinin and substance P are pro-inflammatory vasoactive peptides; accumulation causes vasodilation and vessel edema (Slides 38-39).
correlates.treatment: stop the drug. Angioedema of any cause is an absolute contraindication to all RAS inhibitors (Slide 40).

correlates.name: RAS Inhibitor Acute Kidney Injury and Hyperkalemia
correlates.pathophysiology: efferent arteriolar dilation drops glomerular capillary pressure. If intrarenal perfusion pressure is already compromised, that further drop causes acute kidney injury.

correlates.name: Olmesartan Sprue-Like Enteropathy
correlates.presentation: severe chronic diarrhea and weight loss.
correlates.pathophysiology: a drug-specific effect unique to olmesartan, not a class effect of the ARBs (Slide 38).

correlates.name: Fetal RAS Inhibitor Toxicity
correlates.pathophysiology: fetal renal function depends on angiotensin II; RAS blockade produces fetal hypotension and anuria with depressed renal function (Slide 40).
correlates.treatment: prevention only. Absolutely contraindicated in all trimesters, for every RAS inhibitor - period, the end .

drugs.name: Captopril
drugs.mechanism: Competitively inhibits ACE, so angiotensin I is not converted to angiotensin II and bradykinin is not degraded; it is one of the two ACE inhibitors that is not a prodrug
drugs.indication: Hypertension, HFrEF, post-MI remodeling and proteinuric chronic kidney disease — though its short half-life forces 2-3 times daily dosing
drugs.adverseEffects: Dry cough in 5-20%, angioedema, hyperkalemia, first-dose hypotension and a fall in GFR; absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy

drugs.name: Enalapril
drugs.mechanism: A prodrug hydrolyzed by hepatic and intestinal esterases to enalaprilat, the active ACE inhibitor — and the only member of the class with an intravenous form
drugs.indication: Once-daily hypertension and heart failure therapy, with enalaprilat available when the intravenous route is required
drugs.adverseEffects: Class effects of cough, angioedema, hyperkalemia and reduced GFR; fetal hypotension, anuria, oligohydramnios and skull malformation in pregnancy

drugs.name: Lisinopril
drugs.mechanism: ACE inhibition without prodrug conversion, given once daily with a half-life that lengthens in the elderly
drugs.indication: First-line hypertension, HFrEF alongside a beta blocker and loop diuretic, and slowing progression of proteinuric CKD
drugs.adverseEffects: Dry cough from accumulated bradykinin, substance P and prostaglandins in the lung; angioedema; hyperkalemia

drugs.name: Losartan
drugs.mechanism: Competitive high-affinity antagonism at the AT1 receptor, leaving angiotensin II free to stimulate the vasodilating, natriuretic AT2 receptor and raising renin release
drugs.indication: Hypertension and proteinuric CKD in the patient who cannot tolerate an ACE inhibitor cough
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyperkalemia and reduced GFR as with ACE inhibitors, but little cough; angioedema rates no higher than non-RAS drugs

drugs.name: Olmesartan
drugs.mechanism: AT1 receptor blockade with once-daily oral dosing and no intravenous form available in the class
drugs.adverseEffects: A sprue-like enteropathy unique to this ARB — severe chronic diarrhea and weight loss — on top of the class hyperkalemia

drugs.name: Sacubitril-Valsartan
drugs.mechanism: Pairs neprilysin inhibition, which raises natriuretic peptides, bradykinin and substance P, with AT1 receptor blockade
drugs.indication: HFrEF, where the combined natriuretic and RAS-blocking effect outperforms an ACE inhibitor alone
drugs.adverseEffects: Hypotension and hyperkalemia, with angioedema risk that forbids overlapping it with an ACE inhibitor

drugs.name: Aliskiren
drugs.mechanism: Potent selective competitive renin inhibition that blocks angiotensinogen from reaching the active site, so no angiotensin I is ever formed
drugs.indication: An alternative agent for hypertension only — never first-line, and never combined with an ACE inhibitor or ARB
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyperkalemia and hypotension, worse below a creatinine clearance of 30 mL/min; only about 3% bioavailable and sensitive to P-glycoprotein inducers and inhibitors

formulas.name: Blood Pressure
formulas.equation: BP = Cardiac Output x Peripheral Vascular Resistance
formulas.meaning: Every antihypertensive drug works by lowering one of these two terms, which is why the drug classes sort onto four control sites: resistance arterioles, capacitance venules, the heart and the kidneys
formulas.normalValue: Under 120/80 mm Hg; stage 1 is 130-139 systolic or 80-89 diastolic, stage 2 is 140/90 or above

formulas.name: Cardiac Output
formulas.equation: CO = Stroke Volume x Heart Rate
formulas.meaning: The volume of blood the heart ejects per minute, and the term that beta blockers and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers attack
